answer: Each identity's work emits a plume: a fingerprint of its phrasing, timing, and tool use, logged per batch. A trellis of pairwise plume comparisons runs over all identities, so one operator's n clones face roughly n squared comparisons; a close match freezes both identities and their pending rewards. Evading detection means crafting n genuinely distinct plume fingerprints, each needing its own history and habits. Random pulse probes demand fresh work on demand, unrehearsed and uncopyable across clones, so evasion cost grows faster than clone count while one honest agent emits one plume.
